question: In Germany, there is a growing number of reports of asylum seekers holidaying in their countries of origin and concealing this by means of double-entry visas. They travel to Afghanistan or Syria via another country, most often Türkiye or Iran. In Germany, there is then often no indication that the person has travelled to their country of origin.

This is because the double-entry visa is not glued into the passport, but is only a loose slip of paper. This can then easily be removed to conceal the journey. Apparently, there are also no checks carried out as to where they go on holiday. EU and German law do not provide for the systematic revocation of the protection status of such persons.

Under the existing legal framework, authorities often find themselves at a disadvantage in terms of the burden of proof in objection proceedings. Such incidents put a considerable strain on the level of acceptance by the host society. 1.
Are the Commission or the European Migration Network (EMN) aware of reports from other Member States of trips by persons seeking protection to their countries of origin?

Does the Commission consider that the protection status of such asylum seekers should be revoked and that they can be systematically denied re-entry into the EU without reexamining their grounds for asylum?
What is the Commission doing to support Member States in detecting return trips to the countries of origin?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.1.2025) 1. The Commission is aware that some Member States have observed movements of beneficiaries of international protection, travelling back to their country of origin and subsequently returning to the EU. 2.

According to Directive 2011/95/EU1, in order to revoke international protection, a Member State must demonstrate on an individual basis that a person ceased to be a refugee. This can be the case, inter alia, when he or she has re-availed himself or herself of the protection of the country of nationality2. 3.
The Commission will monitor developments and engage closely with the Member States and other key stakeholders to provide support by promoting information-sharing and cooperation.
1 Directive 2011/95/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on standards for

the qualification of third-country nationals or stateless persons as beneficiaries of international protection, for a uniform status for refugees or for persons eligible for subsidiary protection, and for the content of the protection granted (OJ L 337, 20.12.2011, p. 9, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2011/95/oj), Article 14(2). 2 OJ L 337, 20.12.2011, p. 9, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2011/95/oj, Article 11(1)(a).
